tlsDependency.name: Mbed TLS
tlsDependency.license: Apache-2.0 (selected from upstream Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later)

changes: Optional HLS_ENABLE_TLS build switch defaults OFF; published executables include the statically linked backend; runtime remains HTTP by default
--https with PEM/DER certificate chain and matching private key, or --tls-self-signed for an in-memory per-run RSA-2048 certificate with local DNS/IP SANs and fingerprint

TLS1.2/1.3 only, ECDHE with preferred AEAD suites and trailing AES128-CBC-SHA256 compatibility suites for Win7 Schannel, HTTP/1.1 ALPN, renegotiation disabled, TLS1.3 PSK-only exchange/early data not enabled
Bounded asynchronous mbedTLS BIO over existing socket strands; 16KiB encrypted input, at most64KiB queued encrypted output, no dedicated thread per connection
Separate handshake ceiling32 and absolute timeout10s; process-local one-hour encrypted session tickets and TLS close-notify
std::mutex mbedTLS threading adapters protect shared PSA, RNG and key state across socket strands
Actual transport scheme drives CSRF Origin, hotlink Referer, Secure cookies, preview CSP, URL/QR advertisement and MCP download URLs
Configured private key path/physical aliases cannot be served or overwritten through shared roots/native mounts; webpage operations cannot delete or rename its parent
Pinned official offline source archive and SHA256, fetch script, selected Apache-2.0 license embedded by TLS builds, source-compatible Windows7+/musl/macOS code

windows: MSVC static runtime TLS-enabled build; CTest3/3
Real HTTPS suite: exact TLS1.2 and1.3, TLS1.1 rejection, ALPN, trusted/untrusted temporary certificate, IP SAN, verified RSA and ECDSA supplied certificates, DER parse
96 HTTPS Range operations using24 concurrent workers, range beyond4GiB in5GiB sparse file, multi-record ranges, repeated Keep-Alive
TLS session ticket resumption and clean close-notify checked by a client rejecting ragged EOF
Streaming fixed/chunked uploads, chunked gzip download, exact payloads, fragmented ClientHello/records/HTTP
HTTPS CSRF/Referer, Secure HttpOnly cookie, authenticated sandbox preview and related CSS, HTTPS MCP and URL/QR
Key download/replacement denied for original/hardlink/native mount paths, parent rename/delete denied, mismatched credentials rejected before serving
Handshake parallel cap and absolute timeout reclaim stalled connections
Existing HTTP core/144 ranges/backpressure/Server, login/hotlink/compression/QR/access, COW writer/reader/move and branding suites pass
Final dist zero-argument HTTP8000 defaults and embedded TLS Apache license checked
Forced TLS1.2 ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 with P256 negotiates the documented Win7 Schannel cipher subset (not an IE/Win7 engine run)
linuxMusl: Static stripped x86_64 TLS-enabled build; CTest3/3
Same full HTTPS suite passed using older Python/OpenSSL clients, including supplied DER keys, trust/SAN, resumption, clean TLS shutdown, concurrency, private-key aliases and handshake budgets
Existing HTTP core/144 ranges/backpressure/Server and access/login/hotlink/compression suite passed
Same forced Win7 Schannel cipher subset negotiation passed
tlsOff: Separate MSVC build with HLS_ENABLE_TLS=OFF compiled without mbedTLS libraries
HTTP session request passed; --tls-self-signed exits with an explicit rebuild instruction
javascript: 21 frontend/vendor ES5 sources plus embedded login script static IE compatibility checks passed; frontend unchanged
verification.ie11: No actual IE/Win7 HTTPS run. TLS1.2 capabilities and certificate trust must be validated on the target system.
verification.macos: Source compatibility only; no build or test per user instruction

limits: Current listener selects HTTP or HTTPS; no simultaneous protocol sniffing, extra HTTP redirect listener, HTTP/2 or QUIC
Temporary certificate changes per run, is valid30days and requires explicit client trust; app never installs roots or changes browser protections
Certificate/key are loaded only at startup; encrypted private keys and client-certificate authentication are not implemented
TLS has per-connection memory/CPU cost; existing global connection/transfer ceilings remain relevant
Key copies made as independent files cannot be recognized by physical identity; keep credentials and backups outside the shared tree
